verdict.rationale: Lovable's docs claim you can send follow-ups, corrections, or new ideas at any time to steer ongoing work (docs-30) and that Build/Agent mode 'takes ownership of execution end to end' (docs-4/18/29), implying iterative prompting is safe and managed. However, independent community reports describe concrete breakage from AI-generated changes/backend logic — a flawed RPC access-control implementation that blocked legitimate users and exposed data to unauthenticated ones (comm-7), and a case where accumulated iteration produced an unmaintainable, slow architecture that had to be rebuilt elsewhere (comm-13) — directly contradicting the 'without breaking what already works' promise. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of regression protection, versioning/rollback safety nets for iterative edits, and independent confirmation that follow-up prompts reliably preserve prior functionality.
